name: The Hated
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two St. John's College faculty kids in Annapolis name a band from a kibbutz, play church basements and a school playground for five years, then plug back in about 35 years later.

eras.title: A name dreamed up on a kibbutz
eras.text: Erik Fisher and Daniel Littleton grew up with fathers teaching at the same college. They start with Beatles covers played faster and louder, then aim at the hardcore scene 30 miles away in Washington.

years.big: "By calling ourselves The Hated, it was sort of a dare"
years.h: Two faculty kids in Annapolis start a band
years.p: Erik Fisher and Daniel Littleton, whose fathers both taught at St. John's College, begin as the Dead Beatles, playing Beatles songs faster and distorted. Fisher comes up with the name during a stay on a kibbutz in Israel.
years.xp:
Fisher pictured the name on an American flag and sent it to Littleton by letter, according to Tone Glow. Fisher's own line on it: "By calling ourselves The Hated, it was sort of a dare. Like, we dare you to dig this."

Before the Hated there were Fit of Rage and Geek Patrol. Two early songs, "Touch It" and "No Meaning," went on a 1984 local compilation while Fisher was away; Littleton called them "like a love letter of sorts to Erik," per Gebhardt, a bid to get him home.

Wikipedia lists MDC, the Minutemen and Annapolis's Spastic Rats as early touchstones.

years.h: They play wherever Annapolis lets them, even under a pendulum
years.p: Church basements, a playground behind an elementary school, the pendulum stairwell at St. John's College: the Hated take any room that will have them.
years.xp:
Gebhardt describes the playground show, summer 1985, for "maybe 10-15" people, and acoustic sets in the St. John's stairwell, where a Foucault pendulum hangs and the reverb is cavernous.

Fisher also ran a zine, CRAB, short for Citizens for the Reeducation of the Annapolis Bourgeoisie. The scene's other anchor was the Annapolis Record Exchange. Littleton, per Tone Glow: "We didn't have an after school program, we had the Annapolis Record Exchange."

yt: "I Don't Like You" from the tape (audio)
years.h: First on tape: The Best Piece of Shit Vol. 3
years.p: Fisher sings and plays guitar, Littleton plays bass, Colin Meeder plays guitar and Mike Bonner drums, on a release the band puts out itself.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates it to 1985 and lists it as self-released. Decades later the Numero Group's Ken Shipley and Littleton dug up earlier and rougher material, going back to 1983-84, for a Vol. 4.

eras.title: The label boss takes the drum stool
eras.text: Kenny Hill runs Vermin Scum out of Annapolis and drums for the Spastic Rats. He puts out the Hated's records, then joins them.

years.h: No More We Cry is the Hated's first record on Vermin Scum
years.p: A 7-inch cut at LSP Studios in Annapolis, for the label run by the man who is about to become the band's drummer.
years.xp:
LSP was an 8-track studio in the Hillsmere basement of Les Lentz, who recorded the first wave of Annapolis hardcore, including the Spastic Rats and Moss Icon, per Gebhardt. The band reportedly still owes him money from those sessions.

Gebhardt counts six songs on the 7-inch. Tone Glow singles out "Rubber Bullets," an acoustic song about apartheid.

years.h: Hill swaps the label for the drum kit
years.p: Kenny Hill, who had been releasing the band on Vermin Scum and drumming for the Spastic Rats, takes the stool from Mike Bonner.

years.cap: The Hated live in a graffiti-covered room, c. 1986
yt: Title song live at Numero Twenty, Los Angeles, 2023
years.h: What Was Behind, put out by the band itself
years.p: A 1986 release with no label behind it, wedged between the Vermin Scum 7-inch and the next EP.
years.xp: The Numero Group's Bandcamp page for the catalog lists the record. The band played its title song again, 37 years on, at Numero Twenty in Los Angeles on February 19, 2023.

years.cap: Erik Fisher, Daniel Littleton, Kenny Hill and a friend in the band's tour van, 1987
years.h: Like the Days lands, and the band hits the road in a van
years.p: The second Vermin Scum record, the last before Fisher's return to college slows the band down.

eras.title: Last album, last show
eras.text: Fisher goes back to school, the band makes one more album, and the original Hated stop in Maryland.

years.h: Every Song closes out the Vermin Scum run
years.p: The original band's last studio album, made as Erik Fisher resumes his college studies.

years.h: The last show is in Crofton, Maryland
years.p: Summer 1989: Fisher, Littleton and Hill finish five years of church basements. Littleton goes on to form Ida with Elizabeth Mitchell.
years.xp:
Littleton told the Washington Post, "We got through it. And that was the last time we played." Wikipedia gives no more detail on the Crofton show.

Gebhardt notes Littleton later formed Three Shades of Dirty with Meeder.

eras.title: Awl, on a Simple Machines tape
eras.text: Simple Machines collects the scattered 1985 to 1988 recordings on a cassette for its Tool series.

years.h: Awl gathers the old tapes for Simple Machines
years.p: Sixteen tracks, mostly cut at LSP Studios between summer 1985 and winter 1987-88, on the label's Tool Cassette Series.
years.xp: Discogs lists Meeder and John Irvine sharing bass duties and Bonner and Hill both on drums. One Discogs reviewer says some copies were badly dubbed, which cut off the starts of songs.

eras.title: A drummer lost, an archive found
eras.text: Littleton builds Ida while the old tapes sit in the dark. Hill dies in 2020, and the reissue work starts after.

years.h: Kenny Hill dies in Brooklyn Park, Maryland
years.p: The drummer who founded Vermin Scum and joined the band in 1985 was 55, according to Wikipedia. He missed the reunion by about three years.

eras.title: Numero digs it up
eras.text: The Numero Group reissues the archive, and the band plays again for the first time in about 35 years.

years.h: The Numero Group unearths The Best Piece of Shit, Vol. 4
years.p: Ken Shipley and Daniel Littleton assemble unreleased early Hated material, some of it from before the name, 1983-84.

years.cap: Daniel Littleton (center) with Miggy Littleton and Jason Fisher, January 2023
yt: Full set, Earleigh Heights Fire Hall, 2023
years.h: The Hated play again, and the show runs 90 minutes late
years.p: Fisher, Littleton, Meeder, Bonner and John Irvine are joined by Jason Fisher and Miggy Littleton, who drums in Hill's place.
years.xp:
The January 15 show was at the Earleigh Heights fire hall in Severna Park, after three days of practice, per Tone Glow. The Washington Post reports speaker glitches, unplugged cables and dead vocal monitors, and a set that ran past the midnight curfew.

A month later they played Numero Twenty in Los Angeles, on a bill with Unwound, Codeine and Everyone Asked About You, per Wikipedia.

years.p: More recordings from the old tapes, put out by the Numero Group.
